A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, problem, and core contributions. Their complete main texts and appendices A–E provide readable equations, figures, tables, and proofs sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic optimization, insulin-dosage simulation, and inverted-pendulum experiments, including regret curves and sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical studies, revises reported results, and adds insulin-dosage results for Thompson-sampling variants.

M1.justification: Appendix E.3 introduces AdveRS-G-TS, with Algorithm 3 and Equation 39. It samples a function from the GP posterior and selects actions by minimizing its p-fragility, adding a distinct randomized exploration procedure to v1's UCB-based algorithm family.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic objective, UVA/PADOVA insulin-dosage task, and inverted-pendulum controller task. Random, LCB, worst-case, and kernel-misspecification scenarios already appear in v1. The new Thompson-sampling evaluation reuses the insulin task.

E2.justification: RS-G with p=2 is added to the retained insulin, inverted-pendulum, and misspecified-kernel comparisons; Table 2 also gains an RSG row. Figure 10 adds Thompson-sampling variants. STABLEOPT and its experiment-specific radius variants remain the external comparators.

E3.justification: The misspecified RBF kernel's stated lengthscale and variance change from 1 and 1 to 0.1 and 10. Section 5 corrects attack objectives to evaluate perturbed inputs, and Gaussian perturbation laws now use squared standard deviations. These are revisions to reported settings; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing kernel-misspecification analysis is reconfigured and extended to RS-G with p=2, while Table 2 adds RSG to the threshold/radius sensitivity study. These expand evidence about kernel robustness and parameter sensitivity. The increasing-perturbation robustness analysis was already present in v1.

E5.justification: v1 states that all experiments average 100 runs. v2 explicitly reports 20 runs for Table 2 and the new Thompson-sampling results, while retaining 100 runs for other curves. The std/2 error-bar convention remains unchanged. This establishes changed run-count reporting, not an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: Numerous regret curves and all existing Table 2 values change; for example, RS2 at tau=-10 changes from 0.72 to 185.39. RSG and Thompson-sampling results are added. Figure 3b no longer shows p=2 as best under LCB and worst-case attacks, and the pendulum finding changes from outperforming to matching correctly specified STABLEOPT. Revised settings and unclear aggregation prevent treating these as comparable performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 revises Lemma 3.1's confidence-width formula, makes fragility nonnegative, corrects the kernel metric, and adds a strict-inclusion condition to Corollary 3.5. It also corrects the generalized regret's fragility parameter and expands proofs in Appendices C.1, C.2, and C.8. These are substantive local revisions to existing theory rather than new regret theorems.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and central conclusion retain the same claims: two robust-satisficing formulations unified by RS-G, their regret guarantees, and advantages when RO ambiguity sets are misspecified. The Thompson-sampling extension is not incorporated into the main contribution claims.

C2.justification: New Remark 2.3 explains why arbitrary adversarial perturbations differ from distribution-based VaR, CVaR, and DRO formulations. The conclusion newly identifies observing realized perturbations as an applicability limitation and proposes unobserved perturbations as future work.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds a code-repository link absent from v1. The insulin discussion now explicitly gives the negative absolute-deviation reward, and revised kernel hyperparameters are documented. Appendix D's discretized implementation and quadratic acquisition-cost description remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Thompson's original paper and Russo et al.'s Thompson-sampling tutorial as references 45–46. Remark 2.3 also clarifies positioning relative to probabilistic robustness. The remaining bibliography largely retains the same works; the GP-UCB preprint-to-publication update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized corrections and explanations, expanded affiliations, the new robustness remark, and appendix reorganization accommodating Thompson sampling and moving existing empirical material into the main text.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout and extensively revises empirical displays, including axes and legends. Synthetic RS-regret plots move into main-text Figure 4, separate insulin plots become paired Figure 5, and new Figure 10 displays Thompson-sampling comparisons. Algorithm 3 and the expanded Table 2 further change the presentation.

improvement.justification: Corrected fragility and kernel formulas, clearer applicability limits, a code link, and the documented Thompson-sampling alternative provide a modest improvement in precision and usability. Important weaknesses remain: Table 2's large scale change is unexplained, the retained p=2-best statement conflicts with revised Figure 3b, and Appendix C.8 asserts uniform convergence without establishing it.
